clue.text: Post stuff on voicemail?

indicators.note: a voicemail message is heard rather than read, so the word for stuff is taken as spoken

parts.note: to stuff is to cram or jam

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to post their belongings by leaving a phone message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on voicemail?' says the word is heard: JAM (cram) is spoken the same as the door-frame upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Prize fish has to sink

parts.note: a jack is a fish, a young pike among others
to pot a ball in snooker or pool is to sink it

explanation.surface: A fish won as a prize is destined for the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the top prize in a lottery or gaming machine.

clue.text: Spiritual teacher has to embrace religious subject, greeting mother superior

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means placed above the rest, so the mother goes on top

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it as in a hug

parts.note: taken as written
RI, religious instruction, is a school subject
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A guru greets a mother superior and embraces a point of theology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother superior' looks like a nun's title; in a down clue 'superior' simply means placed on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual leader, a title made famous by the Beatles' guru.

clue.text: Sees, once again, house prices close to unaffordable dismissed

parts.note: bis is a musical direction meaning repeat, once again

indicators.note: the letter is sent away from the word prices

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: House prices yet again rise beyond reach and lose their audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to unaffordable' is E, which 'dismissed' removes from PRICES to leave PRICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, so sees are bishoprics, the areas a bishop governs.

clue.text: Fix single stone, cutting round figure

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

indicators.note: the stone abbreviation is put into the round figure, splitting it

parts.note: nil, zero, is a round figure shaped like an O
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A mason trims a single stone around a circular statue.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to fix it firmly in someone's mind.

clue.text: Nazi touring country finds Venus

indicators.note: the Nazi's name goes all round the country, as a tourist circles it

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi
Peru is a South American country

explanation.surface: A German fascist travels around abroad and discovers a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperus is the evening star, a classical name for the planet Venus seen at dusk.

clue.text: Cipher gone as it unravels a shade

indicators.note: a code that unravels comes apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secret code falls apart and turns into a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'unravels', acting on CIPHER GONE AS IT, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistachio green is a pale yellowish-green colour named after the nut.

clue.text: Top of eyelashes found at the bottom of a hip bone

indicators.note: the top of the word is its first letter, which is the one that moves
in a down clue, the letter shifted to the bottom goes to the end

parts.note: cilia is the anatomical word for eyelashes

explanation.surface: A stray eyelash ends up low down, on a hip bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of' and 'found at the bottom' move the C of CILIA from its start to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac is the adjective for the ilium, the large upper bone of the pelvis, so it means relating to a hip bone.

clue.text: Figure that winger's broken bone

indicators.note: the figure is broken open by the bird going into it

parts.note: a sum is a figure, a total
a tern is a seabird, a winger; the 's is read as has

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing has broken a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer; it is a bird, the tern, which 'broken' sets inside SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Was Dracula so old?

parts.note: the idiom for being old is read literally about a vampire, whose fangs are prominently long teeth

explanation.definitionFit: Long in the tooth is an idiom meaning old, from horses' gums receding with age.

clue.text: Chelsea's leadership a laugh, ending in tedious league

indicators.note: the leadership of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hoot is a laugh

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Chelsea's management have a laugh as the tedious league drags on.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in league, cahoots meaning a partnership or collusion.

clue.text: Full of sulphur, phosphorus and iodine, safe to breathe

indicators.note: the word for safe is filled with the chemical symbols

parts.note: sure means safe, secure
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemist asks whether air laden with three elements is safe to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspire is a literary verb meaning to breathe or sigh.

clue.text: Bird has to go off circling say in long river, blue

indicators.note: the error-and-example piece is placed inside the word for long

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: the word for go off wraps round the abbreviation for say

parts.note: to err is to go off course, astray
EG, for example, means say
the Fal is a river in Cornwall
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory, CON

explanation.surface: A bird flies off, circling a long river under a blue sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, and blue is the Conservative party colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a bird of prey, famous as the fastest diving bird.

clue.text: Infusion from can not quite all there

indicators.note: the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
someone all there is sane, of sound mind

explanation.surface: A drink from a tin is a bit off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion of herbs or flowers in hot water, a herbal tea.

clue.text: Corn needs space to grow rapidly

parts.note: mush is a porridge of cornmeal, in American usage
room is space

explanation.surface: A farmer's corn needs room to spread fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to spring up or expand quickly, like the fungus appearing overnight.

clue.text: Position of chairman having made a splash

definitions.meaning: a chairman sits over the board of directors
something gone over the side of a ship lands in the water with a splash

explanation.definitionFit: Overboard means over the side of a ship into the sea; split, over board places a chairman above the directors.

clue.text: Husband en route to ruin, up to this point

indicators.note: the words are ruined, wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband on his journey is bound for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ruin' is the anagram signal for EN ROUTE, giving EREUNTO after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereunto is a formal adverb meaning to this place or point, up to now.

clue.text: Son, having lost weight, is now this?

definitions.text: Son, having lost weight, is now this?

parts.note: a person who has shed weight is lighter

explanation.surface: A boy has dieted and wonders how to describe himself now.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighter means slimmer, more slender, as a son who has lost weight would be.

clue.text: It's taken up both sides of rider on a horse

definitions.text: It's taken up both sides of rider on a horse

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive dropped

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a jockey who is up is on a horse

explanation.surface: A piece of tack is pulled up on each side of someone in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns ITS into STI; 'both sides of' gives RR from rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup hangs at each side of a horse's saddle and is pulled up when not in use.

clue.text: Stick with firm at present

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to remain loyal to the present company.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together, holding as a unified whole.

clue.text: On entering terribly neat, such is the answer

definitions.text: On entering terribly neat, such is the answer

indicators.note: the cricket side goes inside the rearranged letters
something done terribly is botched, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A solver admires a reply that slots in tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also the leg side, a convention worth knowing; the definition reads the answer as an admiring verdict on the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means pleasingly neat and ingenious, as a stylish solution is.

clue.text: I've resolved to eat animal produce? No!

definitions.text: I've resolved to eat animal produce? No!

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it, as food is eaten
letters resolved are broken down and reassembled in another order

parts.note: an egg is produce from an animal

explanation.surface: Someone tempted by animal products firmly refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'No!' is the vegetarian's refusal, which is why the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie, a vegetarian, refuses to eat animal flesh.

clue.text: Dictator I haven't suggested anagrammatically?

parts.note: the first two words of the name are an anagram of I haven't, and the third word is a typical anagram signal, so the name reads as an instruction

explanation.surface: A tyrant denies having put forward a rearrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: IVAN THE is an anagram of I HAVEN'T, and TERRIBLE is the sort of word that signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia, the first tsar, was an autocrat known for cruelty, a dictator in effect.

clue.text: With credit account taken over, start to accumulate capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the account sits on top of the credit
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: With a credit account taken over, a firm begins to build capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' puts AC above CR in this down clue; it is not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: American native took flight about the speed of light — gosh!

indicators.note: the word for took flight goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ran means fled, took flight
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light
coo is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: A Native American fled at light speed, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: COO is a British exclamation of surprise. 'American native' suggests a person; it is an animal native to America.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a masked mammal native to North America.

clue.text: A European king beginning to gravitate to the West Caribbean island

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a Dane is a European
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A European monarch is drawn westward to a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the West' reverses the whole run ADANERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the southern Caribbean.

clue.text: Nobody in literature maintains English has developed as a weapon

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Charles Pooter is the hero of The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith

indicators.note: letters developed are worked into a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary nonentity insists the English have built a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a comic Victorian novel, whose nobody is Charles Pooter. 'developed' turns HAS into ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube for blowing dried peas, a child's weapon.

clue.text: That which provides entrance to pithead, I think

indicators.note: the answer is found within the following words, attached to them

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a shaft gives access to the top of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage giving access into a mine.
